newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - BTP vols firm on unease at futures rally.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - BTP vols firm on unease at futures rally.

text.p: Implied volatility of Italian BTP options on LIFFE was firm to slightly higher on Thursday as concerns that futures may be overvalued started to circulate, traders said.
BTP futures set a new record high at 133.65, around 10 full points above the lows of the year in March and April.
The September contract was up 32 basis points on the day at 132.40 at 1038 GMT.
"Most of the trades are still bullish but a pull back has got to be a possibility," said a trader at a British brokerage on the LIFFE floor.
"I could see a two point clear out in the futures quite quickly, and volatility at at least 8.5 percent would be the consequence."
September options volatility was at 7.50 percent, up from 7.36 bid at 7.60 offered at the open.

Major trades included a U.S. bank which bought 2,000 lots of the 134.00, 136.00 call spreads. The 136.00 calls were bought outright at a volatility of 7.09 percent, and 500 lots of the 132.00 puts were bought at 7.80 percent vol.
A trader at a French house said activity in high upside calls was heavy indicating expectations of further upside potential for the futures despite the already meteoric rise.
"We've even seen the 140.00 calls going through," said the French bank trader. "Yesterday they were really rocking and today there is still steady interest."
Around 500 lots of the 140.00 September calls had been traded by 1040 GMT.

Traders said they started to get uneasy about the strength of the underlying futures when the 10-year BTP/Bund yield spread set a new record low on Wednesday fell further to 122 basis points on Thursday.
"The spread looks like a sell at these levels and it could be the trigger for futures to take stock," said a trader at a European bank.
